Namespace: PDFSolid_Conversion.Common Assembly: .dll Syntax public enum ErrorCode Fields Name Description e_ErrCancel Cancel conversion. e_ErrCompress Folder compression failed. e_ErrConverting Currently executing conversion task. e_ErrExpire The resource (e.g., license, token) has expired. e_ErrFile File cannot be found or could not be opened. e_ErrIO System IO error occurs. e_ErrImageDataEmpty The image data is empty or not provided. e_ErrImageInvalid The image is invalid or corrupted. e_ErrImageUnsupportedFormat The image format is not supported (e.g., not RGB, YUV, etc.). e_ErrImageWHError The image width or height is invalid (e.g., less than or equal to zero). e_ErrInvalidArg Invalid argument provided. e_ErrInvalidHandle The handle is invalid, possibly uninitialized or already released. e_ErrInvalidTable The table data is invalid or null. e_ErrLibraryNotLoad Current library has not been loaded yet. e_ErrLicenseConcurrencyExceeded The current conversion concurrency exceeds the license limit. e_ErrLicenseExpire The license has expired. e_ErrLicenseFileReadFailed Failed to read license file. e_ErrLicenseIllegalAccess Illegal access to the API interface. e_ErrLicenseInvalid The license is invalid. e_ErrLicenseMismatch The license does not match the device, module, or version. e_ErrLicenseOCRPermissionDeny The license does not have OCR permissions. e_ErrLicensePageLimitExceeded The current conversion pages exceed the license limit. e_ErrLicensePermissionDeny The license does not have the function permission. e_ErrLicenseQuotaCorrupted The quota persistence file has been tampered with. e_ErrLicenseUninitialized License has not been initialized. e_ErrLicenseUnsupportedAPI The current license does not support calling this API. e_ErrLicenseUnsupportedDevice The license does not support the device id. e_ErrLicenseUnsupportedID The license does not support the application id. e_ErrLicenseUnsupportedPlatform The license does not support the current platform. e_ErrMissingArg A required argument is missing. e_ErrModelFormatUnsupported The model format is not supported by this system or SDK. e_ErrModelFunctionUnsupported The model does not support the requested function or operation. e_ErrModelInvalidFormat The model file format is invalid or corrupted. e_ErrModelSDKMismatch The model is incompatible with the current SDK version. e_ErrNoTable There are no tables in the PDF document. e_ErrOCRFailure OCR recognition failed. e_ErrOutOfMemory Out-of-memory error occurs. e_ErrPDFFormat Format is invalid. For files, this may also mean that file is corrupted. e_ErrPDFPage PDF page not found or content error. e_ErrPDFPassword Invalid password. Usually, this error may occur when loading a PDF document with password. When meet this, user should load document again with correct password. e_ErrPDFSecurity PDF document is encrypted by some unsupported security handler. e_ErrSuccess Success, and no error occurs. e_ErrUnknown Any unknown error occurs. e_ErrUnsupportedFeature The source document uses a feature this SDK cannot fully reproduce, or the requested output cannot carry the input's content. A usable output may still have been written: Word to PDF normally still produces the PDF and reports this in its optional diagnostics.

api/PDFSolid_Conversion.Common.LibraryMa.summary: Class LibraryManager Manages all operations related to the SDK library. The LibraryManager class manages the lifecycle of the SDK library: loading the native library, initializing it with resources, verifying licenses, loading and releasing DocumentAI models, setting the number of DocumentAI models, counting pages in documents, querying the remaining page quota, retrieving version information, and releasing resources. Declaration public static void ReleaseDocumentAIModel() SetDocumentAIModel(string, int) Loads DocumentAI components from a model package, used for OCR, layout analysis and table recognition. Each call loads only the capabilities contained in the given model package and merges them with the capabilities already loaded; it does not replace them. If a package fails to load, the capabilities loaded before are kept. For example, load documentai.model first and then table_legacy.model to enable e_HighAccuracy. Stop new SDK calls and wait for running conversions to finish before calling it. SetDocumentAIModelCount(int, int) Sets the number of DocumentAI models for layout analysis and table recognition. Call it before conversion starts; the call is ignored while conversion tasks are running or a release is pending. Declaration public static ErrorCode StartWordToPDF(string file_path, string output_path, WordOptions options, out string diagnostics, ConvertCallback callback = default) Parameters Type Name Description string file_path The input Word document path. string output_path The output path of the converted PDF file. WordOptions options Conversion options; null uses the defaults. Word to PDF uses only PageRanges and WordPdfBookmarkMode. string diagnostics Receives the diagnostics decoded from the native UTF-8 text, or an empty string when there is nothing to report. The first line is output=produced when the PDF was written or output=not_produced when it was not; each following line names one unsupported feature, reported once per feature. ConvertCallback callback Callback for reporting conversion progress or canceling the operation. Returns Type Description ErrorCode ErrorCode indicating the success or failure of the operation. e_ErrUnsupportedFeature means the document uses features that may affect fidelity; the PDF is usually still produced, which the first diagnostics line confirms. e_ErrOutOfMemory means the diagnostics did not fit in the native 8192-byte buffer. A real conversion failure returns its own error code, which takes precedence. Remarks Only native libraries built with Word to PDF support export this entry point. Call IsWordToPDFSupported() after the library is loaded to find out.

getting-started.html.title: Getting Started | PDFSolid Conversion SDK
getting-started.html.summary: Getting Started Deploy and initialize Reference lib/pdfsolidconversionsdk_dotnet.dll from the 1.3.0 SDK. Keep the matching native DLLs from lib/x64 or lib/x86 together and set your project to the corresponding process architecture. Do not mix x86 and x64 DLLs or use an older native SDK with the 1.3.0 managed assembly. Call LibraryManager.InitLibrary with the directory containing the native DLLs, then call LibraryManager.Initialize with the SDK resource directory. Verify a valid Windows license before converting. Stop on a load, initialization, or license failure. For the shipped x64 demo, open PDFSolid_Conversion_Demo.sln in Visual Studio. Use its x64 configuration and provide your Windows license.xml next to the executable. The project copies the x64 native DLLs and resources to the output directory. Convert Word (DOCX) to PDF Check IsWordToPDFSupported() on the loaded native library before converting. The example uses x64, resource, and license.xml next to the application; use x86 instead when deploying an x86 application. Supply an existing DOCX and a writable output path. using System; using System.IO; using PDFSolid_Conversion.Common; using PDFSolid_Conversion.Conversion; string appDir = AppDomain.CurrentDomain.BaseDirectory; if (!LibraryManager.InitLibrary(Path.Combine(appDir, "x64"))) throw new InvalidOperationException("Could not load the x64 native SDK."); try { if (!LibraryManager.Initialize(Path.Combine(appDir, "resource"))) throw new InvalidOperationException("Could not initialize SDK resources."); ErrorCode license = LibraryManager.LicenseVerify(Path.Combine(appDir, "license.xml")); if (license != ErrorCode.e_ErrSuccess) throw new InvalidOperationException("License verification failed: " + license); if (!CPDFConversion.IsWordToPDFSupported()) throw new NotSupportedException("The loaded native SDK does not expose Word to PDF."); var options = new WordOptions { PageRanges = "1-2", WordPdfBookmarkMode = WordPdfBookmarkMode.e_Headings }; string diagnostics; ErrorCode result = CPDFConversion.StartWordToPDF("input.docx", "output.pdf", options, out diagnostics); if (result == ErrorCode.e_ErrUnsupportedFeature) Console.Error.WriteLine(diagnostics); // Check output=produced or output=not_produced before using the PDF. else if (result != ErrorCode.e_ErrSuccess) throw new InvalidOperationException("Conversion failed: " + result); } finally { LibraryManager.Release(); } Omit WordOptions for all pages with no bookmarks. Word to PDF does not require loading a DocumentAI model. For supported options, the diagnostics overload and result handling, see the Word to PDF API and the Word to PDF guide. For PDF input, see the Conversion Guides and CPDFConversion class.

introduction.html.title: Introduction | PDFSolid Conversion SDK
introduction.html.summary: Introduction PDFSolid Conversion SDK 1.3.0 for Windows (.NET) supports both PDF export and Word (DOCX) to PDF. Conversion capabilities PDF to Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), PowerPoint (.pptx), HTML, CSV, images, plain text, RTF, JSON, and Markdown. PDF to Searchable PDF and OFD, with OCR and transparent text options where applicable. Word (.docx) to PDF via StartWordToPDF. Select page ranges and optionally create PDF bookmarks from headings or Word bookmarks. Legacy .doc is not supported by this entry point. Supported images can also be used as input for image conversion, including frame-by-frame conversion of multi-page TIFF. See Getting Started for deployment and your first conversion, the developer guide for workflows and options, and the CPDFConversion API for signatures and return codes.
